newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond market focuses on new issues.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond market focuses on new issues.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond market players focused primarily on the large number of new corporate bond issues to price on Wednesday, as trading activity in the secondary market remained fairly quiet, traders said.
In the investment-grade sector, General Motors Acceptance Corp, the financial services unit of General Motors Corp, sold $1 billion in five-year bonds in its first global offering.
Traders said spreads on the bonds tightened by one basis point from a when-issued spread of 42 basis points in after-market trading.
Merrill Lynch & Co and J.P. Morgan Securities Inc co-lead managed the deal.

Other large issues to hit the market on Wednesday included a $450 million offering of 10- and 30-year notes from Baxter International via Goldman Sachs & Co; a $500 million issue of 30-year debentures from GTE Corp via Goldman; and a $300 million offering of 30-year bonds from Eastman Chemical Co via Merrill Lynch.
Traders said spreads of outstanding investment-grade bonds widened by one to three basis points on average, as the market struggled to digest the new supply.

Elsewhere, TCI Communications Inc bonds widened by 20 basis points late on Wednesday on rumors that the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) had downgraded the company's debt rating.
The rumors triggered spread widening across the cable sector, traders said.
The NAIC later confirmed downgrading TCI debt to an NAIC-3 from an NAIC-2 rating.
The move followed a decision by Standard & Poor's last week to affirm TCI's BBB-minus debt rating after an extensive review.
In the high-yield market, secondary market prices were unchanged to lower by 1/4 of a point on a day of light trading, traders said.

Issuers to tap the market included Supermercados Norte, a Latin American supermarket company, which sold $220 million in junk bonds; and Collins & Aikman Floorcoverings Inc which sold $100 million in notes via BT Securities Inc.
Both deals priced on the inside of price talk, signifying strong investor demand, traders said.

In the secondary market, prices of PIK exchangeable preferred stocks continued to weaken due to concerns about an oversupply of such securities in recent weeks, traders said. The U.S. Treasury market ended higher on Wednesday after the U.S. Treasury's first indexed note sales attracted strong bidding.
The price of the benchmark 30-year long bond rose by 7/32 to end the day at 94-27/32, yielding 6.91 percent.
